01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_1_P.title: Print Hello, World
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_1_P.summary: Shows the greeting Hello, World! on the screen.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_1_P.analogy: It is like a newborn's first word: the simplest possible proof that the computer can hear you and speak back.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_1_P.watchFor: Watch the single line of text appear in the output the moment the print step runs.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_2_P.title: Print your name, class and roll on separate lines
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_2_P.summary: Prints a student's name, class and roll number, each on its own line.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_2_P.analogy: Think of filling in the three lines of a school ID card, one line at a time from top to bottom.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_2_P.watchFor: Notice how each endl pushes the next piece of text onto a fresh line.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_3_P.title: Print a small ASCII box
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_3_P.summary: Draws a small rectangle on the screen using plus signs, dashes and bars.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_3_P.analogy: It is like drawing a box on graph paper line by line: a top edge, two sides, then a bottom edge.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_Class_3_P.watchFor: Watch the box take shape as the four lines stack up one under another.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_1_Prin.title: Print your daily timetable
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_1_Prin.summary: Prints a simple school timetable with times and subjects.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_1_Prin.analogy: It is like copying your class timetable onto the first page of a new notebook, one period per line.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_1_Prin.watchFor: Notice that the computer prints the lines in exactly the order they are written, top to bottom.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_2_Prin.title: Print a 4-line ASCII figure
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_2_Prin.summary: Draws a little house-like shape with slashes, underscores and bars.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_2_Prin.analogy: It is like making a picture with matchsticks on a table: each line of text adds another layer of sticks.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L1_HW_2_Prin.watchFor: Watch how the double backslash in the code shows up as a single backslash on screen.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_1_D.title: A variable of each type
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_1_D.summary: Stores an age, a population, the value of pi, a grade letter, a yes/no answer and a name, then prints them all.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_1_D.analogy: Variables are like labelled kitchen containers: a small jar for salt, a big drum for rice, each sized for what it holds.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_1_D.watchFor: Notice how each box gets filled with its value first, and how the true value prints as 1.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_2_A.title: Area and perimeter of a rectangle
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_2_A.summary: Works out how much space a rectangle covers and how long its border is.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_2_A.analogy: Area is how many tiles you need to cover a floor, and perimeter is how much ribbon you need to go around its edge.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_2_A.watchFor: Watch area and perimeter get calculated from length and breadth before anything is printed.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_3_S.title: Swap two numbers using a third variable
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_3_S.summary: Exchanges the values of two numbers with the help of a spare box.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_3_S.analogy: To swap the drinks in two full glasses, you first pour one into an empty third glass so nothing spills.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_Class_3_S.watchFor: Follow the three moves: a goes into temp, b goes into a, then temp goes into b.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_1_Prin.title: Size of each data type
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_1_Prin.summary: Shows how many bytes of memory each kind of value takes up.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_1_Prin.analogy: It is like checking the size of each container on a shelf: a tiny pouch for one letter, a bigger box for a long number.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_1_Prin.watchFor: Notice that a char takes just 1 byte while a long long or double takes 8.

01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_2_Cels.title: Celsius to Fahrenheit converter
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_2_Cels.summary: Converts body temperature from Celsius to Fahrenheit using a formula.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_2_Cels.analogy: It is like a currency exchange counter: you hand over a value in one unit and get the same amount back in another.
01_Getting_Started_with_Cpp/L2_HW_2_Cels.watchFor: Watch 37 get multiplied by 9, divided by 5, then increased by 32 to become 98.6.

02_Operators/L1_Class_1_Last_digit_and_f.title: First and last digit of a number
02_Operators/L1_Class_1_Last_digit_and_f.summary: Picks out the first and the last digit of a four-digit number.
02_Operators/L1_Class_1_Last_digit_and_f.analogy: Dividing by 10 and keeping the remainder is like tearing the last coupon off a strip, while dividing by 1000 keeps only the first coupon.
02_Operators/L1_Class_1_Last_digit_and_f.watchFor: Notice how % 10 gives the last digit and / 1000 throws away everything except the first.

02_Operators/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_digits_of.title: Sum of digits of a 3-digit number
02_Operators/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_digits_of.summary: Splits a three-digit number into its hundreds, tens and units and adds them up.
02_Operators/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_digits_of.analogy: It is like breaking a 573 rupee amount into hundred-rupee notes, ten-rupee notes and coins, then counting the pieces.
02_Operators/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_digits_of.watchFor: Watch how hundreds, tens and units are each pulled out with / and % before being added.

02_Operators/L1_Class_3_Evaluate_a_mixed.title: Evaluate a mixed expression and verify it
02_Operators/L1_Class_3_Evaluate_a_mixed.summary: Calculates a + b * c - a / b and then checks the answer by doing it step by step.
02_Operators/L1_Class_3_Evaluate_a_mixed.analogy: Like the BODMAS rule from school maths: multiplication and division jump the queue before addition and subtraction.
02_Operators/L1_Class_3_Evaluate_a_mixed.watchFor: Notice that 7 / 3 gives 2, not 2.33, because whole-number division drops the leftover.

02_Operators/L1_HW_1_Total_seconds_to_h_.title: Total seconds to hours, minutes and seconds
02_Operators/L1_HW_1_Total_seconds_to_h_.summary: Turns a large number of seconds into hours, minutes and seconds.
02_Operators/L1_HW_1_Total_seconds_to_h_.analogy: It is like packing loose sweets: first fill full boxes of 3600, then smaller packets of 60, and whatever is left stays loose.
02_Operators/L1_HW_1_Total_seconds_to_h_.watchFor: Watch the remainder from each division get passed on to the next smaller unit.

02_Operators/L1_HW_2_Simple_interest_cal.title: Simple interest calculator
02_Operators/L1_HW_2_Simple_interest_cal.summary: Calculates the interest earned on a deposit using principal, rate and time.
02_Operators/L1_HW_2_Simple_interest_cal.analogy: It is like a bank fixed deposit: the extra money you get grows with how much you put in, the rate, and how many years you wait.
02_Operators/L1_HW_2_Simple_interest_cal.watchFor: Notice the formula P times R times T divided by 100 being worked out in one line.

02_Operators/L2_Class_1_Read_two_numbers.title: Sum, difference and product of two numbers
02_Operators/L2_Class_1_Read_two_numbers.summary: Asks for two numbers and prints their sum, difference and product.
02_Operators/L2_Class_1_Read_two_numbers.analogy: It is like a shopkeeper's calculator: you key in two numbers and it shows all three answers at once.
02_Operators/L2_Class_1_Read_two_numbers.watchFor: Watch the two typed numbers land in a and b, then get combined three different ways.

02_Operators/L2_Class_2_Read_radius_prin.title: Area of a circle from its radius
02_Operators/L2_Class_2_Read_radius_prin.summary: Asks for a radius and prints the area of that circle.
02_Operators/L2_Class_2_Read_radius_prin.analogy: It is like working out how much dough you need for a round pizza of a given size.
02_Operators/L2_Class_2_Read_radius_prin.watchFor: Notice that the radius is multiplied by itself, so doubling it makes the area four times bigger.

02_Operators/L2_Class_3_Read_3_marks_pri.title: Total and average of 3 marks
02_Operators/L2_Class_3_Read_3_marks_pri.summary: Takes marks in three subjects and prints the total and the average.
02_Operators/L2_Class_3_Read_3_marks_pri.analogy: It is like a class teacher filling your report card: add up the marks, then share them equally across the subjects.
02_Operators/L2_Class_3_Read_3_marks_pri.watchFor: Watch the total get built first and then divided by 3 to give the average.

02_Operators/L2_HW_1_Bill_price_x_quanti.title: Bill amount with 2 decimal places
02_Operators/L2_HW_1_Bill_price_x_quanti.summary: Multiplies the price of an item by the quantity and prints the bill neatly with two decimals.
02_Operators/L2_HW_1_Bill_price_x_quanti.analogy: It is like a supermarket billing counter that always shows rupees and paise, such as 148.50.
02_Operators/L2_HW_1_Bill_price_x_quanti.watchFor: Notice how fixed and setprecision(2) make the answer always show exactly two digits after the point.

02_Operators/L2_HW_2_Read_a_3_digit_numb.title: Sum of digits of a number you enter
02_Operators/L2_HW_2_Read_a_3_digit_numb.summary: Asks for a three-digit number and prints the sum of its digits.
02_Operators/L2_HW_2_Read_a_3_digit_numb.analogy: It is like taking a three-digit lock code and adding up the numbers on each wheel.
02_Operators/L2_HW_2_Read_a_3_digit_numb.watchFor: Watch the typed number get split into hundreds, tens and units before they are added.

02_Operators/L3_Class_1_Print_whether_a_.title: Print whether a > b
02_Operators/L3_Class_1_Print_whether_a_.summary: Checks whether one number is bigger than another and prints true or false.
02_Operators/L3_Class_1_Print_whether_a_.analogy: It is like a referee comparing two players' heights and simply saying yes or no.
02_Operators/L3_Class_1_Print_whether_a_.watchFor: Notice that boolalpha makes the answer print as the word true instead of 1.

02_Operators/L3_Class_2_Leap_year_as_a_b.title: Leap year as a true/false check
02_Operators/L3_Class_2_Leap_year_as_a_b.summary: Checks in one line whether the year 2024 is a leap year.
02_Operators/L3_Class_2_Leap_year_as_a_b.analogy: It is like a calendar maker's rule card: every fourth year gets an extra day, except century years, unless they divide by 400.
02_Operators/L3_Class_2_Leap_year_as_a_b.watchFor: Watch how the && and || pieces each turn into true or false before combining into the final answer.

02_Operators/L3_Class_3_Is_a_character_a.title: Is a character a vowel?
02_Operators/L3_Class_3_Is_a_character_a.summary: Checks whether a letter is a vowel and prints true or false.
02_Operators/L3_Class_3_Is_a_character_a.analogy: It is like a guard with a list of ten names, small and capital vowels, checking whether the visitor is on the list.
02_Operators/L3_Class_3_Is_a_character_a.watchFor: Notice that as soon as one comparison matches, the whole check becomes true.

02_Operators/L3_HW_1_Voting_eligibility_.title: Voting eligibility as true/false
02_Operators/L3_HW_1_Voting_eligibility_.summary: Decides whether a person can vote based on age and citizenship.
02_Operators/L3_HW_1_Voting_eligibility_.analogy: It is like a polling booth officer who lets you in only if you are 18 or older and also an Indian citizen.
02_Operators/L3_HW_1_Voting_eligibility_.watchFor: Watch how both conditions must be true for the && to give true.

02_Operators/L3_HW_2_Print_the_truth_tab.title: Truth tables of && and ||
02_Operators/L3_HW_2_Print_the_truth_tab.summary: Prints every result of combining true and false with AND and with OR.
02_Operators/L3_HW_2_Print_the_truth_tab.analogy: AND is like a door with two locks that opens only if both keys turn, while OR is a door with two entrances where either one works.
02_Operators/L3_HW_2_Print_the_truth_tab.watchFor: Notice that AND is true only once in four rows, while OR is false only once.

03_If_Else/L1_Class_1_Odd_or_even.title: Odd or even
03_If_Else/L1_Class_1_Odd_or_even.summary: Checks whether a number is odd or even.
03_If_Else/L1_Class_1_Odd_or_even.analogy: It is like pairing up students for a dance: if someone is left without a partner, the count is odd.
03_If_Else/L1_Class_1_Odd_or_even.watchFor: Watch the remainder after dividing by 2 decide which branch the program takes.

03_If_Else/L1_Class_2_Eligible_to_vote.title: Eligible to vote
03_If_Else/L1_Class_2_Eligible_to_vote.summary: Asks for your age and tells you whether you can vote.
03_If_Else/L1_Class_2_Eligible_to_vote.analogy: It is like a gatekeeper at a polling booth who checks your age and either lets you in or asks you to wait.
03_If_Else/L1_Class_2_Eligible_to_vote.watchFor: Notice that with age 17 the condition is false, so the program jumps to the else part.

03_If_Else/L1_Class_3_Maximum_of_two_num.title: Maximum of two numbers
03_If_Else/L1_Class_3_Maximum_of_two_num.summary: Finds the bigger of two numbers.
03_If_Else/L1_Class_3_Maximum_of_two_num.analogy: It is like holding two mangoes, one in each hand, and picking the heavier one.
03_If_Else/L1_Class_3_Maximum_of_two_num.watchFor: Watch the single comparison a > b decide which number gets printed.

03_If_Else/L1_HW_1_Positive_negative_or_.title: Positive, negative or zero
03_If_Else/L1_HW_1_Positive_negative_or_.summary: Tells you whether the number you enter is positive, negative or zero.
03_If_Else/L1_HW_1_Positive_negative_or_.analogy: It is like a thermometer reading: above zero is warm, below zero is freezing, and exactly zero sits on the line.
03_If_Else/L1_HW_1_Positive_negative_or_.watchFor: Notice how the program checks greater than zero first, and only then tries less than zero.

03_If_Else/L1_HW_2_Divisible_by_5.title: Divisible by 5
03_If_Else/L1_HW_2_Divisible_by_5.summary: Checks whether the number you enter can be divided by 5 with nothing left over.
03_If_Else/L1_HW_2_Divisible_by_5.analogy: It is like packing chocolates into boxes of 5: if none are left loose, the number divides evenly.
03_If_Else/L1_HW_2_Divisible_by_5.watchFor: Watch the remainder n % 5 come out as 0 and send the program into the if branch.

03_If_Else/L2_Class_1_Maximum_of_three.title: Maximum of three numbers
03_If_Else/L2_Class_1_Maximum_of_three.summary: Finds the biggest of three numbers using decisions inside decisions.
03_If_Else/L2_Class_1_Maximum_of_three.analogy: It is like a mini knockout tournament: the first two play, and the winner then plays the third.
03_If_Else/L2_Class_1_Maximum_of_three.watchFor: Follow the path: a loses to b in the first check, then b is compared with c.

03_If_Else/L2_Class_2_Grade_from_marks_A.title: Grade from marks (A, B, C, F)
03_If_Else/L2_Class_2_Grade_from_marks_A.summary: Turns your marks out of 100 into a grade letter.
03_If_Else/L2_Class_2_Grade_from_marks_A.analogy: It is like walking down a staircase of cut-offs: you stop at the first step your marks can reach.
03_If_Else/L2_Class_2_Grade_from_marks_A.watchFor: Notice that 82 fails the 90 check but passes the 75 check, so the grade becomes B and the rest are skipped.

03_If_Else/L2_Class_3_Triangle_type_from.title: Triangle type from its sides
03_If_Else/L2_Class_3_Triangle_type_from.summary: Decides whether a triangle is equilateral, isosceles or scalene from its three sides.
03_If_Else/L2_Class_3_Triangle_type_from.analogy: It is like sorting sticks: all three the same length, just two matching, or all different.
03_If_Else/L2_Class_3_Triangle_type_from.watchFor: Watch the very first check succeed because all three sides are 5, so the other checks never run.

03_If_Else/L2_HW_1_Largest_of_three_dist.title: Largest of three distinct numbers
03_If_Else/L2_HW_1_Largest_of_three_dist.summary: Asks for three different numbers and prints the largest.
03_If_Else/L2_HW_1_Largest_of_three_dist.analogy: It is like a talent judge asking each contestant in turn: are you better than both of the others?
03_If_Else/L2_HW_1_Largest_of_three_dist.watchFor: Notice that a fails, b passes both comparisons, and the program never needs to check c.

03_If_Else/L2_HW_2_Calculator_using_if_e.title: Calculator using if-else
03_If_Else/L2_HW_2_Calculator_using_if_e.summary: Reads a simple sum like 12 * 4 and prints the answer.
03_If_Else/L2_HW_2_Calculator_using_if_e.analogy: It is like a cashier who looks at the sign you wrote and then decides whether to add, subtract, multiply or divide.
03_If_Else/L2_HW_2_Calculator_using_if_e.watchFor: Watch the program test the operator against +, then -, then finally match *.

03_If_Else/L3_Class_1_Leap_year_with_bra.title: Leap year with branching
03_If_Else/L3_Class_1_Leap_year_with_bra.summary: Asks for a year and works out whether it is a leap year using step-by-step checks.
03_If_Else/L3_Class_1_Leap_year_with_bra.analogy: It is like a three-question quiz at a calendar office: divisible by 4, then by 100, then by 400.
03_If_Else/L3_Class_1_Leap_year_with_bra.watchFor: Notice that 1900 passes the 4 and 100 checks but fails the 400 check, so it is not a leap year.

03_If_Else/L3_Class_2_Classify_a_charact.title: Classify a character: vowel, consonant, digit or other
03_If_Else/L3_Class_2_Classify_a_charact.summary: Tells you whether the character you type is a digit, a vowel, a consonant or something else.
03_If_Else/L3_Class_2_Classify_a_charact.analogy: It is like a post office sorting letters into bins: numbers here, vowels there, other letters in a third bin, and odd items in the last.
03_If_Else/L3_Class_2_Classify_a_charact.watchFor: Watch k skip the digit and vowel checks before landing in the consonant branch.

03_If_Else/L3_Class_3_Is_a_point_inside_.title: Is a point inside a rectangle?
03_If_Else/L3_Class_3_Is_a_point_inside_.summary: Checks whether a point you give lies inside a 10 by 5 rectangle.
03_If_Else/L3_Class_3_Is_a_point_inside_.analogy: It is like checking whether a cricket ball landed inside the boundary rope, both across and along the field.
03_If_Else/L3_Class_3_Is_a_point_inside_.watchFor: Notice that x = 4 is fine, but y = 7 is taller than the height 5, so the point is outside.

03_If_Else/L3_HW_1_Ticket_price_by_age_g.title: Ticket price by age group
03_If_Else/L3_HW_1_Ticket_price_by_age_g.summary: Asks for an age and prints the matching ticket price.
03_If_Else/L3_HW_1_Ticket_price_by_age_g.analogy: It is like a zoo ticket counter with a price board: toddlers free, children cheap, adults full price, seniors a discount.
03_If_Else/L3_HW_1_Ticket_price_by_age_g.watchFor: Watch age 8 skip the under-5 rule and match the 5 to 12 group for Rs 50.

03_If_Else/L3_HW_2_Valid_triangle_and_it.title: Valid triangle and its type
03_If_Else/L3_HW_2_Valid_triangle_and_it.summary: Checks whether three sides can form a triangle and, if so, what kind it is.
03_If_Else/L3_HW_2_Valid_triangle_and_it.analogy: It is like trying to build a triangle from three sticks: any two together must be longer than the third, or the ends will not meet.
03_If_Else/L3_HW_2_Valid_triangle_and_it.watchFor: Notice that 5, 5 and 8 pass the validity test, then two equal sides make it isosceles.

04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_1_Calculator_usi.title: Calculator using switch
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_1_Calculator_usi.summary: Reads a simple sum like 18 / 4 and prints the answer, jumping straight to the right operation.
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_1_Calculator_usi.analogy: It is like a lift: you press the button for your operator and it goes directly to that floor without stopping at others.
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_1_Calculator_usi.watchFor: Watch the switch jump straight to the / case, check that b is not zero, then break out.

04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_2_Day_of_the_wee.title: Day of the week from a number
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_2_Day_of_the_wee.summary: Turns a number from 1 to 7 into the name of a weekday.
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_2_Day_of_the_wee.analogy: It is like a row of numbered lockers, each holding one day's name; you open the locker matching your number.
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_2_Day_of_the_wee.watchFor: Notice how the program lands directly on case 5 and the break stops it from printing more days.

04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_3_Vowel_check_us.title: Vowel check using switch
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_3_Vowel_check_us.summary: Tells you whether the letter you type is a vowel or a consonant.
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_3_Vowel_check_us.analogy: It is like a guest list where ten names share the same table: any of the vowels gets the same seat.
04_Switch_Case/L1_Class_3_Vowel_check_us.watchFor: Watch several case labels stacked together all lead to the same vowel message.

04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_1_Menu_driven_progr.title: Menu-driven calculator
04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_1_Menu_driven_progr.summary: Shows a menu, lets you pick an operation, then does it on two numbers.
04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_1_Menu_driven_progr.analogy: It is like ordering at a restaurant: you pick item number 3 from the menu and the kitchen makes just that dish.
04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_1_Menu_driven_progr.watchFor: Notice that choice 3 sends the program to the multiply case, giving 6 times 7.

04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_2_Number_of_days_in.title: Number of days in a month
04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_2_Number_of_days_in.summary: Asks for a month number and prints how many days it has in 2024.
04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_2_Number_of_days_in.analogy: It is like the knuckle trick for remembering months: some are 31, some are 30, and February needs a special leap year check.
04_Switch_Case/L1_HW_2_Number_of_days_in.watchFor: Watch month 2 land in the February case, where the leap year test picks 29 days.

04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_1_Print_the_ASCI.title: ASCII value of a character
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_1_Print_the_ASCI.summary: Shows the secret number the computer uses to store the letter A.
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_1_Print_the_ASCI.analogy: Every letter has a roll number in the computer's class register; capital A's roll number is 65.
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_1_Print_the_ASCI.watchFor: Notice that storing the char in an int box reveals its number, 65.

04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_2_Convert_case_u.title: Convert case using ASCII
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_2_Convert_case_u.summary: Turns a small letter into a capital letter and back again by shifting its number.
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_2_Convert_case_u.analogy: Small and capital letters live on two floors of the same building, exactly 32 rooms apart, so you just move up or down 32.
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_2_Convert_case_u.watchFor: Watch g become G when 32 is subtracted, then turn back into g when 32 is added.

04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_3_Count_vowels_i.title: Count vowels in a string
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_3_Count_vowels_i.summary: Counts how many vowels appear in the phrase Hello World.
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_3_Count_vowels_i.analogy: It is like walking along a row of letter tiles with a clicker, pressing it each time you step on a vowel.
04_Switch_Case/L2_Class_3_Count_vowels_i.watchFor: Notice the count going up only at e, o and o as the loop walks through each letter.

04_Switch_Case/L2_HW_1_Reverse_a_string.title: Reverse a string
04_Switch_Case/L2_HW_1_Reverse_a_string.analogy: It is like reading a word in a mirror: you start from the last letter and copy each one moving left.
04_Switch_Case/L2_HW_1_Reverse_a_string.watchFor: Watch the reversed word grow one letter at a time as the position moves from the end to the start.

04_Switch_Case/L2_HW_2_Check_a_one_word_.title: Check a one-word palindrome
04_Switch_Case/L2_HW_2_Check_a_one_word_.summary: Checks whether the word madam reads the same forwards and backwards.
04_Switch_Case/L2_HW_2_Check_a_one_word_.analogy: It is like folding a paper strip in half and checking that the letters on both sides match up.
04_Switch_Case/L2_HW_2_Check_a_one_word_.watchFor: Notice the first and last letters being compared, then the next pair inward, until the middle is reached.

05_Loops/L1_Class_1_Print_1_N_and_even_n.title: Print 1 to N and the even numbers up to N
05_Loops/L1_Class_1_Print_1_N_and_even_n.summary: Prints all numbers from 1 to 10, then just the even ones.
05_Loops/L1_Class_1_Print_1_N_and_even_n.analogy: The first loop is like climbing every stair, and the second is like taking the stairs two at a time.
05_Loops/L1_Class_1_Print_1_N_and_even_n.watchFor: Notice the second loop starts at 2 and jumps by 2 each time instead of 1.

05_Loops/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_first_N_numbe.title: Sum of first N numbers
05_Loops/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_first_N_numbe.summary: Adds up all the numbers from 1 to 20.
05_Loops/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_first_N_numbe.analogy: It is like dropping coins into a piggy bank: 1 rupee, then 2, then 3, and checking the total at the end.
05_Loops/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_first_N_numbe.watchFor: Watch the sum grow with each round of the loop until it reaches 210.

05_Loops/L1_Class_3_Multiplication_table.title: Multiplication table
05_Loops/L1_Class_3_Multiplication_table.summary: Prints the times table of 7 from 1 to 10.
05_Loops/L1_Class_3_Multiplication_table.analogy: It is like reciting the 7 table in class, one line after another, without writing ten separate lines of code.
05_Loops/L1_Class_3_Multiplication_table.watchFor: Notice that only i changes each round, while 7 stays the same.

05_Loops/L1_HW_1_Print_N_down_to_1.title: Print N down to 1
05_Loops/L1_HW_1_Print_N_down_to_1.analogy: It is like a rocket launch countdown: start high and subtract one each second.
05_Loops/L1_HW_1_Print_N_down_to_1.watchFor: Watch i start at 10 and shrink by one each round until the loop stops after 1.

05_Loops/L1_HW_2_Factorial_with_a_loop.title: Factorial with a loop
05_Loops/L1_HW_2_Factorial_with_a_loop.summary: Multiplies 1 times 2 times 3 up to 6 to get 6 factorial.
05_Loops/L1_HW_2_Factorial_with_a_loop.analogy: It is like counting how many ways 6 friends can stand in a line: 6 choices for first place, 5 for second, and so on.
05_Loops/L1_HW_2_Factorial_with_a_loop.watchFor: Notice how the answer grows very fast, reaching 720 in just six rounds.

06_Patterns/L1_Class_1_Sum_of_digits_and.title: Sum of digits and reverse of a number
06_Patterns/L1_Class_1_Sum_of_digits_and.summary: Adds up the digits of 4527 and also writes the number backwards.
06_Patterns/L1_Class_1_Sum_of_digits_and.analogy: It is like peeling stickers off the right end of a strip one at a time, adding their values and sticking them onto a new strip in reverse order.
06_Patterns/L1_Class_1_Sum_of_digits_and.watchFor: Watch each digit get chopped off the end, added to sum, and pushed onto reversed.

06_Patterns/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_squares_an.title: Sum of squares and alternating series
06_Patterns/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_squares_an.summary: Adds the squares of 1 to 6, then adds and subtracts 1 to 6 by turns.
06_Patterns/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_squares_an.analogy: The first part is like stacking square tiles of growing size; the second is like taking one step forward and one step back, each a bit bigger.
06_Patterns/L1_Class_2_Sum_of_squares_an.watchFor: Notice odd numbers are added and even numbers are subtracted in the second loop.

06_Patterns/L1_Class_3_Number_triangle.title: Number triangle
06_Patterns/L1_Class_3_Number_triangle.summary: Prints a triangle where each row counts from 1 up to the row number.
06_Patterns/L1_Class_3_Number_triangle.analogy: It is like a child learning to count, going one number further on each new try.
06_Patterns/L1_Class_3_Number_triangle.watchFor: Watch the inner loop run one more time on each new row.

06_Patterns/L1_HW_1_Harmonic_series_1_1_.title: Harmonic series 1 + 1/2 + ... + 1/N
06_Patterns/L1_HW_1_Harmonic_series_1_1_.summary: Adds 1, a half, a third, a quarter and a fifth together.
06_Patterns/L1_HW_1_Harmonic_series_1_1_.analogy: It is like sharing one pizza with 1 person, then 2, then 3, and adding up the slice you get each time.
06_Patterns/L1_HW_1_Harmonic_series_1_1_.watchFor: Notice how each piece added gets smaller, so the total grows more and more slowly.

06_Patterns/L1_HW_2_Floyd_s_triangle.title: Floyd's triangle
06_Patterns/L1_HW_2_Floyd_s_triangle.summary: Prints the numbers 1 to 15 in a triangle, one more number in each row.
06_Patterns/L1_HW_2_Floyd_s_triangle.analogy: It is like seating people in a stadium where each row has one more seat, numbering them in order as they arrive.
06_Patterns/L1_HW_2_Floyd_s_triangle.watchFor: Watch num keep counting up across rows instead of restarting at 1.

06_Patterns/L2_Class_1_Single_row_and_si.title: Single row and single column of stars
06_Patterns/L2_Class_1_Single_row_and_si.summary: Prints five stars side by side, then five stars stacked one below another.
06_Patterns/L2_Class_1_Single_row_and_si.analogy: It is like placing five coins in a line on a table, then stacking five coins in a tower.
06_Patterns/L2_Class_1_Single_row_and_si.watchFor: Notice the only difference is where the endl goes: after the loop for the row, inside it for the column.

06_Patterns/L2_Class_2_Solid_square.title: Solid square
06_Patterns/L2_Class_2_Solid_square.summary: Prints a 4 by 4 square made of stars.
06_Patterns/L2_Class_2_Solid_square.analogy: It is like laying floor tiles: finish one full row, then move down and start the next.
06_Patterns/L2_Class_2_Solid_square.watchFor: Watch the inner loop print 4 stars before the outer loop moves to a new row.

06_Patterns/L2_Class_3_Right_angled_tria.title: Right-angled triangle
06_Patterns/L2_Class_3_Right_angled_tria.summary: Prints a triangle of stars where each row has one more star than the last.
06_Patterns/L2_Class_3_Right_angled_tria.analogy: It is like building a staircase out of bricks, adding one more brick on each step.
06_Patterns/L2_Class_3_Right_angled_tria.watchFor: Notice the number of stars in each row is equal to the row number.

06_Patterns/L2_HW_1_Inverted_right_angle.title: Inverted right-angled triangle
06_Patterns/L2_HW_1_Inverted_right_angle.summary: Prints a triangle of stars that starts wide and gets one star shorter each row.
06_Patterns/L2_HW_1_Inverted_right_angle.analogy: It is like a stack of plates where you remove one plate from each new pile.
06_Patterns/L2_HW_1_Inverted_right_angle.watchFor: Watch n - i + 1 shrink from 5 down to 1 as the rows go by.

06_Patterns/L2_HW_2_Solid_rectangle_of_R.title: Solid rectangle of R rows and C columns
06_Patterns/L2_HW_2_Solid_rectangle_of_R.summary: Prints a block of stars 3 rows tall and 6 columns wide.
06_Patterns/L2_HW_2_Solid_rectangle_of_R.analogy: It is like arranging chairs in a hall: 3 rows with 6 chairs in each.
06_Patterns/L2_HW_2_Solid_rectangle_of_R.watchFor: Notice the outer loop controls the rows and the inner loop controls how many stars go in each.

06_Patterns/L3_Class_1_Star_pyramid.title: Star pyramid
06_Patterns/L3_Class_1_Star_pyramid.summary: Prints a centred pyramid of stars that gets wider at the bottom.
06_Patterns/L3_Class_1_Star_pyramid.analogy: It is like stacking cups into a pyramid: each lower row is wider and starts a little further to the left.
06_Patterns/L3_Class_1_Star_pyramid.watchFor: Notice how the spaces shrink by one each row while the stars grow by two.

06_Patterns/L3_Class_2_Inverted_pyramid.title: Inverted pyramid
06_Patterns/L3_Class_2_Inverted_pyramid.summary: Prints an upside-down pyramid of stars that narrows to a single star.
06_Patterns/L3_Class_2_Inverted_pyramid.analogy: It is like a funnel: wide at the top and narrowing down to one point.
06_Patterns/L3_Class_2_Inverted_pyramid.watchFor: Watch the spaces grow by one each row while the stars shrink by two.

06_Patterns/L3_Class_3_Palindromic_numbe.title: Palindromic number pyramid
06_Patterns/L3_Class_3_Palindromic_numbe.summary: Prints a pyramid where each row counts up to the row number and back down, like 12321.
06_Patterns/L3_Class_3_Palindromic_numbe.analogy: It is like climbing up a hill and then walking back down the other side using the same steps.
06_Patterns/L3_Class_3_Palindromic_numbe.watchFor: Notice each row uses two loops: one counting up, then one counting back down.

06_Patterns/L3_HW_1_Right_aligned_triang.title: Right-aligned triangle
06_Patterns/L3_HW_1_Right_aligned_triang.summary: Prints a triangle of stars that leans against the right side.
06_Patterns/L3_HW_1_Right_aligned_triang.analogy: It is like books on a shelf pushed to the right: empty space fills the left side of each row.
06_Patterns/L3_HW_1_Right_aligned_triang.watchFor: Watch spaces and stars always add up to 5 in every row.

06_Patterns/L3_HW_2_Pyramid_using_spaced.title: Pyramid using spaced stars
06_Patterns/L3_HW_2_Pyramid_using_spaced.summary: Prints a pyramid where each row has as many stars as its row number, with gaps between them.
06_Patterns/L3_HW_2_Pyramid_using_spaced.analogy: It is like a group photo with each row of people standing a little apart, and each back row having one more person.
06_Patterns/L3_HW_2_Pyramid_using_spaced.watchFor: Notice that because each star has a space after it, only i stars are needed to make the pyramid shape.

06_Patterns/L4_Class_1_Full_diamond.title: Full diamond
06_Patterns/L4_Class_1_Full_diamond.summary: Prints a diamond of stars by drawing a pyramid and then an upside-down pyramid.
06_Patterns/L4_Class_1_Full_diamond.analogy: It is like two pyramids glued base to base, one pointing up and one pointing down.
06_Patterns/L4_Class_1_Full_diamond.watchFor: Watch the second half start one row shorter so the widest row is not printed twice.

06_Patterns/L4_Class_2_Hollow_square.title: Hollow square
06_Patterns/L4_Class_2_Hollow_square.summary: Prints only the border of a square, leaving the inside empty.
06_Patterns/L4_Class_2_Hollow_square.analogy: It is like a photo frame: solid on all four edges with an empty space in the middle.
06_Patterns/L4_Class_2_Hollow_square.watchFor: Notice that a star is printed only on the first or last row or column; everywhere else gets a blank.

06_Patterns/L4_Class_3_Alphabet_triangle.title: Alphabet triangle
06_Patterns/L4_Class_3_Alphabet_triangle.summary: Prints a triangle of letters where each row goes A, B, C up to the row number.
06_Patterns/L4_Class_3_Alphabet_triangle.analogy: It is like a child reciting the alphabet and getting one letter further on each try.
06_Patterns/L4_Class_3_Alphabet_triangle.watchFor: Watch 'A' + j - 1 turn the numbers 1, 2, 3 into the letters A, B, C.

06_Patterns/L4_HW_1_Hollow_pyramid.title: Hollow pyramid
06_Patterns/L4_HW_1_Hollow_pyramid.summary: Prints only the outline of a star pyramid with an empty inside.
06_Patterns/L4_HW_1_Hollow_pyramid.analogy: It is like a tent seen from the front: two slanting sides and a flat floor, with open space inside.
06_Patterns/L4_HW_1_Hollow_pyramid.watchFor: Notice stars appear only at the first and last spot of each row, except the bottom row which is fully filled.

06_Patterns/L4_HW_2_Alphabet_pyramid.title: Alphabet pyramid
06_Patterns/L4_HW_2_Alphabet_pyramid.summary: Prints a centred pyramid of letters like A, ABA, ABCBA.
06_Patterns/L4_HW_2_Alphabet_pyramid.analogy: It is like a mountain of letters: climb up the alphabet to the peak, then walk back down.
06_Patterns/L4_HW_2_Alphabet_pyramid.watchFor: Watch each row go up the alphabet to the row's letter and then back down to A.

07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_1_Calculate_.title: Time complexity of a simple for loop
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_1_Calculate_.summary: Counts how many times a loop from 1 to N runs, showing that the work grows exactly with N.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_1_Calculate_.analogy: It is like climbing N stairs: 10 stairs means 10 steps, 20 stairs means 20 steps.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_1_Calculate_.watchFor: Watch count go up by one on every pass until it equals N.

07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_2_Calculate_.title: Time complexity of a halving loop
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_2_Calculate_.summary: Keeps cutting 64 in half until it reaches 1 and counts how many cuts it took.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_2_Calculate_.analogy: It is like folding a sheet of paper in half again and again: it gets tiny very quickly.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_2_Calculate_.watchFor: Notice temp shrinks 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 in only 6 passes, far fewer than 64.

07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_3_Differenti.title: O(1) versus O(N)
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_3_Differenti.summary: Adds 1 to N twice: once with a loop that takes N steps, once with a formula that takes one step.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_3_Differenti.analogy: Counting a pile of coins one by one versus reading the total printed on the bag.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_Class_3_Differenti.watchFor: Watch the loop do 8 additions while the formula gets the same 36 in one line.

07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_1_Best_vs_worst.title: Best vs worst case of linear search
07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_1_Best_vs_worst.summary: Searches the same list twice: once for the first item and once for the last, counting comparisons.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_1_Best_vs_worst.analogy: Looking for your friend in a queue: lucky if they stand first, unlucky if they stand last.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_1_Best_vs_worst.watchFor: Notice the first search stops after 1 comparison but the second needs all 6.

07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_2_TC_of_finding.title: Time complexity of finding the maximum
07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_2_TC_of_finding.summary: Finds the biggest number in a list and counts the comparisons it needed.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_2_TC_of_finding.analogy: Like finding the tallest student: you must look at every single student, there is no shortcut.
07_Time_Complexity/L1_HW_2_TC_of_finding.watchFor: Watch maxVal change only when a bigger number shows up, while comparisons ticks every pass.

07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_1_TC_of_nest.title: Nested loops: O(N^2)
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_1_TC_of_nest.summary: Runs a loop inside a loop, both from 1 to N, and counts how often the inner body runs.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_1_TC_of_nest.analogy: Every student in a class shaking hands with every student in another class of the same size.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_1_TC_of_nest.watchFor: Watch j restart from 1 every time i moves on, so count reaches 4 x 4 = 16.

07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_2_TC_of_depe.title: Dependent nested loops
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_2_TC_of_depe.summary: Runs an inner loop that goes only up to i, so each row does a little more work than the last.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_2_TC_of_depe.analogy: Like stacking a staircase of bricks: 1 brick, then 2, then 3, up to N.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_2_TC_of_depe.watchFor: Notice the inner loop runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 times, adding up to 15.

07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_3_TC_of_i_ti.title: Doubling loop: O(log N)
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_3_TC_of_i_ti.summary: Doubles i each time until it passes 100 and prints every value it visits.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_3_TC_of_i_ti.analogy: Like a rumour that doubles the people who know it every hour: it reaches a crowd fast.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_Class_3_TC_of_i_ti.watchFor: Watch i jump 1, 2, 4, 8 ... 64 and the loop finish after only 7 passes.

07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_1_TC_of_three_n.title: Three nested loops: O(N^3)
07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_1_TC_of_three_n.summary: Puts three loops inside each other and counts how often the innermost line runs.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_1_TC_of_three_n.analogy: Like counting every small cube inside a 3 x 3 x 3 Rubik's cube.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_1_TC_of_three_n.watchFor: Watch k cycle fully for every j, and j for every i, giving 27 in total.

07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_2_TC_of_i_plus_.title: i += 2 versus i *= 2
07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_2_TC_of_i_plus_.summary: Runs two loops up to 32, one adding 2 each time and one doubling, and compares their step counts.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_2_TC_of_i_plus_.analogy: Walking two steps at a time versus taking a lift that doubles your floor each ride.
07_Time_Complexity/L2_HW_2_TC_of_i_plus_.watchFor: Notice the adding loop needs 16 passes while the doubling loop needs only 6.

07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_1_SC_of_crea.title: Space used by an array
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_1_SC_of_crea.summary: Creates an array of N numbers, fills it and prints how many bytes it occupies.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_1_SC_of_crea.analogy: Like booking N seats in a cinema: more friends means more seats taken.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_1_SC_of_crea.watchFor: Watch the array boxes fill up one by one, then see 5 ints take 20 bytes.

07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_2_SC_of_basi.title: Stack space of recursion
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_2_SC_of_basi.summary: Adds 1 to N using a function that calls itself and tracks how many calls are waiting at once.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_2_SC_of_basi.analogy: Like a pile of plates: each new call adds a plate, and they come off only when the bottom one is done.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_2_SC_of_basi.watchFor: Watch the call stack grow to 5 frames deep before the answers start coming back.

07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_3_Time_Space.title: Time-space trade-off with prefix sums
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_3_Time_Space.summary: Finds a range sum twice: by looping over the range, and by using a prepared prefix array.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_3_Time_Space.analogy: Like keeping a running total in your expense notebook so you never need to re-add old bills.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_Class_3_Time_Space.watchFor: Notice the prefix array costs extra boxes, but the final answer needs just one subtraction.

07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_1_Calculate_SC_.title: Space used by a matrix
07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_1_Calculate_SC_.summary: Fills a 3 by 4 grid of numbers, prints it and counts how many cells it uses.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_1_Calculate_SC_.analogy: Like a chocolate bar with rows and columns: rows times columns gives the number of pieces.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_1_Calculate_SC_.watchFor: Watch the grid fill row by row until all 12 cells are used.

07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_2_O_1_space_vs_.title: Reverse an array: O(1) vs O(N) space
07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_2_O_1_space_vs_.summary: Reverses a list two ways: by copying it into a new array, and by swapping ends in place.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_2_O_1_space_vs_.analogy: Rewriting a list backwards on a new page versus swapping the cards in your own hand.
07_Time_Complexity/L3_HW_2_O_1_space_vs_.watchFor: Watch left and right walk towards each other, swapping, without any second array.

08_Functions/L1_Class_1_isPrime_n.title: isPrime(n)
08_Functions/L1_Class_1_isPrime_n.summary: Uses an isPrime function to print every prime number from 1 to 20.
08_Functions/L1_Class_1_isPrime_n.analogy: Like a ticket checker at a gate: hand it a number and it answers yes or no.
08_Functions/L1_Class_1_isPrime_n.watchFor: Watch the call jump into isPrime and leave early with false the moment a divisor is found.

08_Functions/L1_Class_2_factorial_n.title: factorial(n)
08_Functions/L1_Class_2_factorial_n.summary: Declares a factorial function above main, defines it below, and prints 0! to 5!.
08_Functions/L1_Class_2_factorial_n.analogy: Like a recipe card: the title on the menu is the declaration, the cooking steps are the definition.
08_Functions/L1_Class_2_factorial_n.watchFor: Notice main calls factorial before its body appears in the file, thanks to the prototype.

08_Functions/L1_Class_3_max_a_b_and_pass.title: max(a, b) and pass by value
08_Functions/L1_Class_3_max_a_b_and_pass.summary: Finds the bigger of two numbers with a function, then shows a function cannot change the caller's variable.
08_Functions/L1_Class_3_max_a_b_and_pass.analogy: Giving a friend a photocopy of your notes: they can scribble on it, your original stays clean.
08_Functions/L1_Class_3_max_a_b_and_pass.watchFor: Watch x become 100 inside tryToChange while p in main stays 17.

08_Functions/L1_HW_1_sumOfDigits_n.title: sumOfDigits(n)
08_Functions/L1_HW_1_sumOfDigits_n.summary: Adds up the digits of 98765 using a function.
08_Functions/L1_HW_1_sumOfDigits_n.analogy: Like emptying a piggy bank coin by coin and adding up what falls out.
08_Functions/L1_HW_1_sumOfDigits_n.watchFor: Notice n shrinks to 0 inside the function but num in main is untouched.

08_Functions/L1_HW_2_isPalindromeNumber_.title: isPalindromeNumber(n)
08_Functions/L1_HW_2_isPalindromeNumber_.summary: Checks whether a number reads the same forwards and backwards.
08_Functions/L1_HW_2_isPalindromeNumber_.analogy: Like the word MADAM: read it from either end and you get the same thing.
08_Functions/L1_HW_2_isPalindromeNumber_.watchFor: Watch reversed get built digit by digit, then compared with the saved original.

08_Functions/L2_Class_1_nCr_using_a_fact.title: nCr using a factorial helper
08_Functions/L2_Class_1_nCr_using_a_fact.summary: Works out how many ways to choose r items from n by calling factorial three times.
08_Functions/L2_Class_1_nCr_using_a_fact.analogy: Like picking 2 players out of 6 for a team: nCr counts every possible pair.
08_Functions/L2_Class_1_nCr_using_a_fact.watchFor: Watch nCr call factorial again and again, each call with its own fresh variables.

08_Functions/L2_Class_2_power_base_exp_w.title: power(base, exp) with a default
08_Functions/L2_Class_2_power_base_exp_w.summary: Raises a number to a power, and uses a default exponent of 2 when none is given.
08_Functions/L2_Class_2_power_base_exp_w.analogy: Like a coffee machine that makes a regular size unless you press a different button.
08_Functions/L2_Class_2_power_base_exp_w.watchFor: Notice power(7) still works: exp quietly takes its default value 2.

08_Functions/L2_Class_3_Area_functions_f.title: Area functions for shapes
08_Functions/L2_Class_3_Area_functions_f.summary: Uses three small functions to work out the area of a circle, a rectangle and a triangle.
08_Functions/L2_Class_3_Area_functions_f.analogy: Like a toolbox with one labelled tool per job instead of one tool for everything.
08_Functions/L2_Class_3_Area_functions_f.watchFor: Watch each call carry its own measurements in and bring one area back.

08_Functions/L2_HW_1_min_max_of_three_vi.title: min/max of three via a function
08_Functions/L2_HW_1_min_max_of_three_vi.summary: Builds maxOfThree and minOfThree out of smaller two-number helpers.
08_Functions/L2_HW_1_min_max_of_three_vi.analogy: Like a knockout tournament: the winner of the first match plays the third player.
08_Functions/L2_HW_1_min_max_of_three_vi.watchFor: Notice maxOfThree calls maxOfTwo twice, once inside the other.

08_Functions/L2_HW_2_isLeapYear_y_return.title: isLeapYear(y) returning bool
08_Functions/L2_HW_2_isLeapYear_y_return.summary: Tests four years with a function that returns true or false for leap years.
08_Functions/L2_HW_2_isLeapYear_y_return.analogy: Like a calendar rule book that answers one question: does February get 29 days?
08_Functions/L2_HW_2_isLeapYear_y_return.watchFor: Watch 1900 fail the century rule while 2000 passes the 400 rule.

08_Functions/L3_Class_1_Reverse_a_number.title: Reverse a number
08_Functions/L3_Class_1_Reverse_a_number.summary: Reverses the digits of a number using a function, including one with trailing zeros.
08_Functions/L3_Class_1_Reverse_a_number.analogy: Like taking books off one shelf and stacking them on another: the last one off ends up first.
08_Functions/L3_Class_1_Reverse_a_number.watchFor: Notice the reverse of 1200 is 21, because leading zeros vanish.

08_Functions/L3_Class_2_Sum_of_digits.title: Sum of digits
08_Functions/L3_Class_2_Sum_of_digits.summary: Adds up the digits of three different numbers using one reusable function.
08_Functions/L3_Class_2_Sum_of_digits.analogy: Like a cashier totalling the coins in each customer's hand, one customer at a time.
08_Functions/L3_Class_2_Sum_of_digits.watchFor: Watch the same function run three times, each time on a fresh copy of the number.

08_Functions/L3_Class_3_Count_digits.title: Count digits
08_Functions/L3_Class_3_Count_digits.summary: Counts how many digits a number has, taking care of the special case 0.
08_Functions/L3_Class_3_Count_digits.analogy: Like counting the floors of a building by removing one floor at a time from the top.
08_Functions/L3_Class_3_Count_digits.watchFor: Notice countDigits(0) returns 1 straight away instead of entering the loop.

08_Functions/L3_HW_1_Palindrome_number.title: Palindrome number
08_Functions/L3_HW_1_Palindrome_number.summary: Checks four numbers for palindromes by comparing each with its reverse.
08_Functions/L3_HW_1_Palindrome_number.analogy: Like checking whether a word looks the same in a mirror.
08_Functions/L3_HW_1_Palindrome_number.watchFor: Watch isPalindrome hand the work to reverseNumber and simply compare the result.

08_Functions/L3_HW_2_Armstrong_number_an.title: Armstrong number and largest digit
08_Functions/L3_HW_2_Armstrong_number_an.summary: Checks whether numbers equal the sum of their digits raised to the digit count, then finds the largest digit.
08_Functions/L3_HW_2_Armstrong_number_an.analogy: Like a secret club where a number gets in only if its powered-up digits add back to itself.
08_Functions/L3_HW_2_Armstrong_number_an.watchFor: Watch 153 become 1 + 125 + 27 = 153, using countDigits and power together.
